questions.question: The Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kutch and Gangetic delta provide ideal conditions for utilising ________energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tidal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kutch, and the Gangetic delta provide ideal conditions for utilizing **tidal energy**.
 
• Tidal energy is a form of hydropower that converts the energy obtained from tides into useful forms of power, mainly electricity.
 
• These regions have significant tidal ranges, which make them suitable for generating tidal energy.
 
• Tidal energy is a renewable source of energy and has the potential to contribute to the energy mix of India.
 
• Unlike solar and wind energy, tidal energy is predictable and consistent, as tides are influenced by the gravitational forces of the moon and sun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tidal energy** is harnessed by constructing tidal barrages, tidal fences, and tidal turbines.
 
• Tidal barrages work similar to dams, where water is trapped during high tides and released during low tides to generate electricity.
 
• Tidal fences and turbines operate like underwater wind turbines, where the movement of water turns the blades to generate power.
 
• India has a vast coastline, which provides ample opportunities for the development of tidal energy projects.
 
• The development of tidal energy can help reduce the dependence on fossil fuels and contribute to sustainable energy solutions.

• Gopala was elected as the ruler by a group of regional chieftains and gained control over the areas of Bihar and Bengal.
 
• He laid the foundation of the Pala dynasty which ruled from the 8th to the 12th century.
 
• The Pala Empire is known for its patronage of Buddhism and the establishment of many Buddhist institutions and structures.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of football players required in a team for a match to start?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7 players**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **7 players** are the minimum number required for a football match to start according to the Laws of the Game.
 
• The Laws of the Game are maintained by the International Football Association Board (IFAB).
 
• Each team can have a maximum of **11 players** on the field, including the goalkeeper.
 
• If a team cannot field at least 7 players at any point during the match, the game is abandoned.
 
• The rule ensures that the game remains competitive and fair, preventing teams from playing with too few players.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **International Football Association Board (IFAB)** was founded in 1886 and is responsible for the Laws of the Game in association football.
 
• The **Laws of the Game** are the codified rules that help govern the sport of football and ensure consistency across all levels of play.
 
• In official competitions, teams are also required to have a specific number of players on the bench as substitutes, typically ranging from **3 to 7 players** depending on the competition rules.
 
• The **goalkeeper** is a crucial position and must be one of the players on the field at all times.
 
• Substitutions can be made during the match to replace tired or injured players, ensuring that a team can maintain at least the minimum number of players required.

questions.question: What function does the public key serve in digital signature verification?

options.text: To calculate the hash value of the message or file content

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To decrypt the digital signature**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The public key is used **to decrypt the digital signature** in digital signature verification.
 
• Digital signatures are created using the sender's private key and can be verified by the recipient using the corresponding public key.
 
• This process ensures the authenticity and integrity of the message or document, confirming that it was indeed signed by the holder of the private key.
 
• Public key cryptography is a fundamental aspect of secure digital communications, enabling trust and security in electronic transactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Digital signatures are widely used in various applications, including software distribution, financial transactions, and legal agreements, to verify the origin and integrity of the data.
 
• The security of digital signatures relies on the difficulty of deriving the private key from the public key, making it computationally infeasible to forge a valid signature without access to the private key.
 
• Public key infrastructure (PKI) supports the issuance, management, and revocation of digital certificates, which bind public keys to the identities of their owners.
 
• Standards such as RSA and DSA are commonly used algorithms for generating digital signatures.
 
• Regulatory frameworks like the eIDAS Regulation in the European Union provide legal recognition and standards for electronic signatures and trust services.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of Directive Principles of State Policy, and also distinguishes it from Fundamental Rights?

options.text: It protects the interest of the individual.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is non-justiciable**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1** is correct because Directive Principles of State Policy are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court.
 
• These principles are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government and aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Directive Principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution of India from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• In contrast, Fundamental Rights are justiciable and enforceable by the courts, provided in Part III of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles are inspired by the Directive Principles given in the Constitution of Ireland and also by the principles of Gandhism.
 
• They aim to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order through justice—social, economic, and political—and to minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities.
 
• Some of the key areas covered by the Directive Principles include the provision for adequate means of livelihood, equitable distribution of wealth, equal pay for equal work for men and women, protection of children and youth, and promotion of educational and economic interests of weaker sections.
 
• While these principles are not enforceable by law, they are fundamental in the governance of the country, and it is the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT applicable to force?

options.text: Force may make an object move
Force may change the direction of a moving object
Force may change the shape of an object
Force may increase the mass of the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Force may increase the mass of the object**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Force may make an object move:** When a force is applied to an object, it can cause the object to start moving if it was initially at rest.
 
• **Force may change the direction of a moving object:** Forces can alter the trajectory of an object in motion, such as a ball being hit in a different direction.
 
• **Force may change the shape of an object:** Applying force can deform objects, such as squeezing a rubber ball.
 
• **Force may increase the mass of the object:** This statement is incorrect. Force cannot change the mass of an object; mass is an intrinsic property of matter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force** is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Newton's second law of motion states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of that object times its acceleration (F = ma).

 
• Forces can be contact forces (e.g., friction, tension) or non-contact forces (e.g., gravity, electromagnetic forces).

 
• Understanding the effects of forces is fundamental in fields such as physics, engineering, and mechanics.

questions.question: ‘Reservation in promotion’ comes under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 16 (4A)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 16 (4A)** of the Indian Constitution deals with reservation in promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
 
• This article was inserted by the **77th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1995**.
 
• It empowers the state to make any provision for the reservation in matters of promotion to any class or classes of posts in the services under the state in favor of the SCs and STs.
 
• The objective is to ensure adequate representation of these communities in public employment.
 
• This provision is aimed at addressing historical injustices and ensuring social equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 16** deals with equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence, or any of them.
 
• However, it allows for exceptions in the form of reservations for backward classes, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes.
 
• The **Constitution (77th Amendment) Act, 1995** was introduced to provide reservations in promotions which were earlier not included under Article 16.
 
• Subsequent amendments like the 85th, 95th, and 117th amendments have further shaped the provisions related to reservation in promotions.

questions.question: Which planet is the second largest planet in our solar system and also has the biggest and brightest rings around it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saturn**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturn** is the second largest planet in our solar system.
 
• It is known for its extensive and bright ring system, which is the most prominent and complex in the solar system.
 
• Saturn is a gas giant, primarily composed of hydrogen and helium.
 
• The planet has at least 274 moons, with Titan being the largest and one of the most interesting due to its thick atmosphere and liquid hydrocarbon lakes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jupiter** is the largest planet in our solar system and also has a ring system, but it is much fainter and less prominent than Saturn's.
 
• Saturn's rings are made up of ice and rock particles that range in size from tiny grains to objects as large as mountains.
 
• The planet's atmosphere exhibits a banded pattern similar to Jupiter's, caused by high-speed winds and differential rotation.
 
• Exploration of Saturn has been primarily conducted by spacecraft such as Pioneer 11, Voyager 1 and 2, and the Cassini-Huygens mission, which provided detailed information about the planet, its rings, and moons.

questions.question: Competitive behaviour and competitive market structure are _______ related.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**inversely**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Competitive behaviour and competitive market structure** are **inversely**__ related.
 
• As the market structure becomes more competitive, the intensity of competitive behaviour among firms tends to decrease.
 
• Conversely, in less competitive market structures, firms are likely to exhibit more aggressive competitive behaviours to gain a larger market share.
 
• This inverse relationship is crucial in understanding market dynamics and the strategic interactions between firms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of market structure and competitive behaviour is fundamental in the field of **industrial organization**.
 
• Market structures can range from **perfect competition** to **monopoly**, with various forms of oligopoly and monopolistic competition in between.
 
• In a perfectly competitive market, firms are price takers and have minimal competitive behaviour regarding pricing.
 
• In contrast, in a monopolistic market, the single firm has significant market power and competitive behaviour can involve barriers to entry and other strategic actions.
 
• Understanding the relationship between market structure and competitive behaviour helps in **regulating markets** and promoting fair competition.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a condition for acquiring the citizenship of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Holding property**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Holding property** is NOT a condition for acquiring the citizenship of India.
 
• Conditions for acquiring Indian citizenship include **domicile, descent, and registration**.
 
• Citizenship can also be acquired by **naturalization** under specific conditions.
 
• The **Citizenship Act, 1955** outlines the various modes and conditions for acquiring Indian citizenship.

• The **Citizenship Act, 1955** provides for acquisition and termination of citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• Citizenship can be acquired by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
• The Act also provides for the renunciation and termination of citizenship.
 
• Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) are provided certain benefits but are not considered Indian citizens.
 
• Recent amendments, such as the **Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019**, have also impacted the criteria and process for acquiring Indian citizenship.
